mismatch_description: The block drops the author's explicit choice of v as a non-cut vertex of G=Γ^c. The author uses the fact that Γ^c is connected with at least 4 vertices to choose a non-cut vertex v, so that Γ\{v} remains irreducible; this non-cut property is part of the corresponding text and is also used later in the proof. The proposition statement only asserts the downstream properties and never records that v is non-cut.
corrected_statement:
Assumptions / Conditions / Definitions.
- The assumptions of Theorem 1 hold.
- n=|\mathcal V(\Gamma)|\geq 4.
- The theorem is assumed to hold for every irreducible graph with k vertices, where 3\leq k<n.
Statement:
Since G=\Gamma^c is connected with at least 4 vertices, there exists a non-cut vertex v\in\mathcal V(\Gamma). Writing \Gamma'=\Gamma\setminus\{v\}, A=M_{\Gamma'}, L=\operatorname{lk}_\Gamma(v), C=M_L, and B=C\overline\otimes M_v, one has
\[
\Gamma'\text{ is irreducible},\qquad A\text{ is properly proximal},\qquad L\subsetneq \mathcal V(\Gamma'),
\]
and
\[
M_\Gamma=A\ast_C B.
\]
corrected_proof:
Since \Gamma^c is a connected graph with at least 4 vertices, it must contain a non-cut vertex v. Thus the induced subgraph \Gamma'=\Gamma\setminus\{v\} remains irreducible and has n-1\geq 3 vertices. By the induction hypothesis, A=M_{\Gamma'} is properly proximal.

Let L=\operatorname{lk}_\Gamma(v). In the complement graph G=\Gamma^c, the vertices of L are exactly the non-neighbors of v. Because v must have at least one neighbor in the connected graph G, the set L is strictly smaller than \mathcal V(\Gamma'). The full graph product M_\Gamma natively decomposes into the amalgamated free product
\[
M_\Gamma=A\ast_C B,\quad\text{where }C=M_L\text{ and }B=C\overline\otimes M_v.
\]
